item.title: Star Families: Greek Myths & Legends — Sat Aug 8, 12:00 PM — Morehead Planetarium and Science Center
item.description:
Gravitate back to Morehead Planetarium for Star Families!
Many of the constellations we can see in our night sky appear as characters in Greek myths. In this immersive planetarium experience, you'll hear tales of monsters, animals, gods, heroes, and princesses while learning to identify the associated constellations.
Star Families is a special series that provides a family-friendly planetarium experience. Arrive before your show or stay after to journey through Morehead's interactive exhibits, science demo spaces, and Cosmic Goods gift shop.
This program is recommended for families and children ages 7+.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: after work bike ride on the ATT — Tue Aug 11, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Triangle Hiking and Outdoors Group We'll be starting near Southpoint and final starting point will be sent out Monday evening.
Make sure that your bike is in good working order - tires hold air and are up to pressure, brakes and shifters work and your chain has been oiled.
We'll be riding just under 2 1/4 hours and about 24 miles. The ride is fairly flat and shaded and our pace will be moderate (about 12 mph average). I recommend a hard tail or hybrid bike, but if you really want to bring a road bike it's ok, though you'll likely be a bit bored. Unicycles....?
I'll be eating after the ride at a restaurant. You're welcome to join me if you like.
Helmets are required and by signing up you agree to THOG liability waiver statement.
Please Note!! Any cancellation less than 30 hours before the beginning of the event will be considered a "no show"
Source: Meetup: Triangle Hiking & Outdoors

item.title: Wilson Library Research Forum — Wed Aug 12, 12:00 PM
item.description:
Each year, scholars from across the nation visit Chapel Hill to conduct research using the rare and historical materials at Wilson Special Collections Library. The Wilson Library Research Forum is an informal program where you can hear from fellowship recipients firsthand and learn about their work with items from the special collections.
In this presentation:
Kathryn Wymer (UNC)
Betty Debnam’s legacy and the future of AI-generated news for children: a digital humanities exploration of the impact of The Mini Page
K. Melchor Hall
Roland L. Freeman (1936 – 2023): (Re)Framing the Legacy of a Photo-Historian of the Black Diaspora
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: Duke Farmers Market — Thu Aug 13, 11:00 AM — None
item.description:
Join us for the Duke Farmers Market! Here you can:
Find farm fresh fruits, vegetables, and other local goods at a convenient location. Enjoy a relaxed atmosphere while learning about local food systems and how eating sustainably can positively impact your health. Support local farmers and independently-owned businesses, including community partners like Duke Campus Farm.
The Duke Farmers Market is an annual market sponsored by LIVE FOR LIFE. LIVE FOR LIFE, Duke's employee wellness program, offers a variety of programs and services, such as health assessments, smoking cessation programs, fitness activities, and health education to help eligible faculty, staff and family members reach health and fitness goals.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Is Your Syllabus Ready? (Online) — Thu Aug 13, 11:00 AM — Virtual
item.description:
Your syllabus is more than a course policy document - it is students' first introduction to your course and a roadmap for their learning. In this interactive workshop, you'll explore practical strategies for creating a syllabus that communicates expectations clearly, supports student success, and sets an inclusive and welcoming tone from the first day of class.
We'll share evidence-informed approaches, syllabus resources, and examples that you can immediately apply as you prepare for the semester. Leave with ideas to strengthen your syllabus and plan a meaningful first day of class. Join us to start the semester strong!
Source: Duke University

item.description:
Health Assessment is a free, confidential health screening provided through Duke benefits. It includes total cholesterol, blood pressure, blood glucose, BMI, waist circumference height, weight and body mass index measurements. Many participants find the coaching session helps them get started making lifestyle changes and connects them to LIVE FOR LIFE and community resources to support them. Health Assessments are available to all active Duke employees.

item.title: Working with Spatial Data in R — Tue Sep 29, 1:00 PM
item.description:
R is a free and open-source way to explore and analyze data, including spatial data. In this workshop, we will introduce you to spatial analysis and visualization techniques in RStudio. We will use packages like sf, tidycensus, tigris, terra, and more to demonstrate typical GIS workflows and produce basic maps.
This workshop is designed for participants with some familiarity with R/RStudio and/or GIS. If you need some additional background, feel free to join our beginR series or our ArcGIS Pro for Beginners workshop earlier in the semester
This workshop is offered by the University Libraries and will be led by librarians Philip McDaniel and Matthew Jansen.
This workshop is being offered remotely via Zoom only. Register here: https://calendar.lib.unc.edu/event/17229736
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.description:
Join Quail Ridge Books as they welcome Mack Paul, coauthor of Miracle Road: The Story of Research Triangle Park. This evening of nostalgia and history will explore the earliest days of Research Triangle Park, the big personalities and big bets that made it a success, and the calvacade of innovations it has gifted to the world. Based on more than 160 interviews with the people who lived, worked, and built RTP into the largest innovation park in America, the book is a must-read for anyone who loves learning about North Carolina history.
Source: NC Humanities Council

**Date, Time and Location**
Oct 08, 2026 9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/mcp-agents-skills-meetup-october-8-2026)**
**Designing Multi‑Agent Systems: Sequential, Parallel, and Beyond with ADK**
Multi‑agent systems are powerful but choosing the wrong interaction pattern can quickly lead to fragile, slow, or expensive AI systems. In this talk, we explore the core multi‑agent design patterns enabled by ADK, including sequential, parallel, and more advanced coordination models. Rather than focusing on tools alone, we’ll look at how to think architecturally about agent collaboration.

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Thu Nov 5 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Thu Nov 5, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources
